Why Jalix

Practical sourcing, handled in a more personal way.

We keep the conversation grounded in what matters: the fabric, the feel, the budget, the quantity and where it needs to go.

01

Requirement-led sourcing

Composition, count, GSM, width, weave, finish and colour direction are captured before supplier matching.

02

Multi-mill flexibility

We can structure options across different manufacturing strengths instead of forcing every requirement into one source.

03

Sampling before scale

Sample review and specification confirmation create a cleaner path from development to bulk ordering.

04

Commercial & shipment coordination

Clear documentation, order milestones and export-ready coordination keep the buying process visible.

Built as a young textile sourcing brandJalix Global Trade started in September 2026 with a clear focus on practical fabric sourcing and export support.
From enquiry to shipment We want every buyer discussion to feel simple, honest and easy to move forward — no unnecessary complexity, just the right fabric and clear execution.
Our vision

To make textile sourcing feel personal, reliable and easier to trust.

Started last month · Growing with purpose

Jalix Global Trade is a new company, but the intention is straightforward: understand what the buyer needs, match it with the right mill, and support the order with clean communication from sampling to shipment.

Instead of looking like a machine-generated catalogue, the brand should feel warm, human and commercial — closer to a real conversation with a sourcing partner.

01

Buyer-first thinking

Every product discussion starts with end-use, hand feel, price expectation and minimum order practicality.

02

Quality with clarity

Construction, composition, width, finish and delivery expectations are shared clearly before bulk commitment.

03

Long-term trade relationships

The goal is not only to sell fabric, but to become a dependable sourcing contact for repeat business.

Jalix promise

Good fabric, clear specification and honest follow-up — that is the kind of business we want buyers to remember.

Construction library

Some of the weaves buyers usually ask us about.

A more visual guide to common fabric directions. Final construction, blend and finish can always be tailored to the requirement.

Poplin

Smooth, clean plain-weave construction used widely for shirts, uniforms and versatile apparel programs.

Clean surface · Light to mid weight

Twill

Diagonal structure that works well for trousers, workwear and durable everyday garments.

Durable drape · Bottomwear friendly

Dobby

Textured woven detail chosen for premium shirting, subtle patterns and elevated fashion surfaces.

Pattern texture · Premium look

Herringbone

Distinctive V-pattern texture for refined shirting, suiting and selected lifestyle collections.

Classic direction · Rich texture

Piqué

Raised textured construction often selected for structured casualwear and comfortable apparel.

Raised texture · Breathable feel

Oxford

Basket-style texture that balances durability with a comfortable premium hand feel.

Structured hand feel · Smart casual

Fil-à-Fil

Subtle two-tone effect that suits clean business shirts and refined apparel stories.

Micro contrast · Elegant surface

Honeycomb

Cellular textured surface that adds visual interest, breathability and useful performance character.

Textured cell structure · Functional appeal
How we work

From requirement to ready-to-ship order.

A simple commercial workflow designed to reduce ambiguity before bulk production.

STEP 01

Brief

Share composition, construction, quantity, target use and commercial expectations.

STEP 02

Source

Relevant mills and products are shortlisted against technical and commercial fit.

STEP 03

Sample

Review swatches or development samples before confirming the bulk direction.

STEP 04

Confirm

Specifications, pricing, quantity, timeline and documentation are aligned.

STEP 05

Ship

Production and shipment milestones are coordinated through final dispatch.

Start a sourcing request

Tell us what fabric you need.

The more specific the brief, the faster the sourcing process. Include end-use, composition, GSM, width, weave, finish, quantity and destination where available.

Typical request: “100% cotton / cotton blend shirting, 120–140 GSM, 58–60 inch width, dobby or twill, bulk requirement for export.”
Thanks — your requirement is ready to be connected to a backend, CRM or email workflow.
